gloss: shaku (traditional unit of length, approx. 30.3 cm)

definitions.gloss: shaku; traditional Japanese unit of length equal to approximately 30.3 cm
definitions.explanation: A traditional unit of length in the Japanese measuring system. One shaku is approximately 30.3 centimeters (about one foot). Still used in traditional architecture, kimono making, and music (shakuhachi).

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{柱|はしら}→柱：05009_hashira⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{八尺|はっしゃく}⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: This pillar is eight shaku tall.

examples.japanese: ⟦{尺八|しゃくはち}→尺八：04465_shakuhachi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一尺八寸|いっしゃくはっすん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{長|なが}さ→長さ：05326_nagasa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{由来|ゆらい}→由来：05451_yurai⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The name shakuhachi comes from its length of one shaku and eight sun.
In the design of Japanese-style rooms, shaku and sun are still sometimes used.

notes:
A traditional unit of length in the Japanese measuring system ({尺貫法|しゃっかんほう}). One {尺|しゃく} is approximately 30.3 cm, roughly equivalent to one foot. Although Japan officially adopted the metric system, the {尺|しゃく} is still used in several traditional fields.

MEASUREMENT SYSTEM:
- ⟦{一寸|いっすん}→一寸：25048_issun⟧ = approximately 3.03 cm
- {一尺|いっしゃく} = 10 {寸|すん} = approximately 30.3 cm
- {一間|いっけん} = 6 {尺|しゃく} = approximately 1.82 m

STILL USED IN:
- ⟦{建築|けんちく}→建築：02709_kenchiku⟧: traditional architecture and tatami sizing
- ⟦{着物|きもの}→着物：01309_kimono⟧: kimono fabric measurements
- ⟦{尺八|しゃくはち}→尺八：04465_shakuhachi⟧: the bamboo flute (named for its standard length)
- ⟦{大工|だいく}→大工：04051_daiku⟧: carpentry

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {尺|しゃく}{貫法|かんほう}: the traditional Japanese measurement system
- {一尺|いっしゃく}: one shaku (about 30 cm)
- {曲尺|かねじゃく}: carpenter's square (using the shaku scale)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寸|すん}: sun — one-tenth of a shaku, approximately 3 cm
- {間|けん}: ken — six shaku, approximately 1.82 m
- ⟦メートル→メートル：02975_meetoru⟧: meter — the modern standard unit
